node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Outcome versus random variable value
node.description: Distinguish an underlying outcome from the numerical value assigned to it by a random variable.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Many outcomes with the same random-variable value
node.description: Recognise when several outcomes map to the same random-variable value and must be combined in the distribution.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Combine probabilities for same value
node.description: Add probabilities of all outcomes that produce the same random-variable value.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Construct distribution from sample space
node.description: Build a discrete probability distribution by mapping each sample-space outcome to a random-variable value and combining matching values.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Support completeness check
node.description: Check that the listed support includes every random-variable value with nonzero probability.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Distribution table ordering
node.description: Order random-variable values in a distribution table so probabilities can be read and accumulated clearly.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Tail probability from distribution table
node.description: Find probabilities such as greater than, less than or at least by summing appropriate entries in a discrete distribution table.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: CDF from distribution table
node.description: Create cumulative probabilities from an ordered discrete distribution table.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Expected value contribution
node.description: Interpret each x times probability term as that value's contribution to the expected value.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Expected value units in context
node.description: State the units of an expected value using the units of the random variable or payoff being modelled.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Net payoff including cost
node.description: Calculate net payoff values by subtracting entry costs or losses before finding expected gain or loss.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Expected gain sign interpretation
node.description: Interpret positive, negative and zero expected gain as favourable, unfavourable or fair in the long run.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Fair price from expected value
node.description: Use expected value to determine a fair entry price or fair payout in a simple chance game.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Compare expected value and spread
node.description: Compare discrete distributions using both expected value and spread when judging long-run outcomes or risk.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Deviation from mean for variance
node.description: Calculate each value's deviation from the mean as a step toward variance of a discrete distribution.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Weighted squared deviation
node.description: Weight squared deviations from the mean by their probabilities when calculating variance.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Standard deviation has original units
node.description: Interpret standard deviation as being in the same units as the random variable, unlike variance.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Same-value outcome probabilities add
node.description: When several outcomes give the same random-variable value, their probabilities are added for that value in the distribution.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Support lists nonzero-probability values
node.description: The support of a discrete random variable lists values that can occur with nonzero probability.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Tail probability sums relevant values
node.description: A discrete tail probability is found by summing probabilities for all values satisfying the inequality.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Expected value has context units
node.description: Expected value is reported in the same units as the random variable or payoff being averaged.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Net payoff before expected gain
node.description: Expected gain should be calculated from net payoffs after accounting for costs, losses or entry prices.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Variance uses weighted squared deviations
node.description: Variance of a discrete random variable is the probability-weighted average of squared deviations from the mean.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Same random-variable values not combined
node.description: Learner lists repeated random-variable values separately instead of combining their probabilities in the distribution.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Tail probability is endpoint only
node.description: Learner uses only the boundary value rather than summing all values in the requested tail event.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Expected gain ignores cost
node.description: Learner calculates expected gain from gross prizes without subtracting entry costs or losses.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Higher expected value always better
node.description: Learner chooses solely by expected value without considering spread, risk or context when those matter.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Variance averages raw deviations
node.description: Learner averages signed deviations from the mean rather than squared deviations weighted by probabilities.

edge.rationale: Constructing a distribution from a sample space is a core way to build a distribution from context.
Tail probabilities are closely related to cumulative probabilities in discrete distributions.
The expected value formula is built from individual x times probability contributions.
Fair price is an application of fair-game expected value reasoning.
Distinguishing outcomes from assigned values builds directly on the meaning of a random variable.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats the outcome and numerical random-variable value as always identical.

edge.rationale: Recognising many outcomes with the same value depends on mapping outcomes to values.
edge.failure_signal: Learner creates repeated rows for the same random-variable value without combining them.

edge.rationale: Combining probabilities follows from recognising multiple outcomes with the same value.
edge.failure_signal: Learner leaves a distribution with duplicate values or probabilities that do not sum correctly.

edge.rationale: Building a distribution from a sample space requires combining probabilities for matching values.
edge.failure_signal: Learner gives a table of raw outcomes rather than a distribution over random-variable values.

edge.rationale: Completeness checks require knowing what the support of a random variable is.
edge.failure_signal: Learner omits possible values with nonzero probability.

edge.rationale: Ordering values is part of making distribution tables easy to read and use.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot accumulate probabilities or identify tails from an unordered table.

edge.rationale: Finding tail probabilities from a table is easier after values are ordered.
edge.failure_signal: Learner includes the wrong side of an inequality or only one endpoint value.

edge.rationale: Cumulative probabilities are built by repeatedly summing probabilities up to a value.
edge.failure_signal: Learner writes individual probabilities instead of cumulative probabilities.

edge.rationale: Interpreting contributions follows from applying the expected value formula.
edge.failure_signal: Learner computes x times probability terms without understanding their role in the sum.

edge.rationale: Expected-value units are interpreted in the same context as the long-run average.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reports expected value as unitless when the random variable has units.

edge.rationale: Expected gain or loss calculations require defining net payoffs before averaging.
edge.failure_signal: Learner ignores entry cost or losses when calculating expected gain.

edge.rationale: Expected gain sign is interpreted after net payoffs are correctly defined.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot connect negative expected gain to long-run loss.

edge.rationale: Fair pricing uses the zero expected-gain condition.
edge.failure_signal: Learner sets a fair price without using the expected gain equals zero idea.

edge.rationale: Comparing expected value and spread builds on comparing distributions by expected value alone.
edge.failure_signal: Learner chooses an option only by mean even when risk or spread matters.

edge.rationale: Variance calculations require first finding the mean or expected value.
edge.failure_signal: Learner calculates deviations from the wrong centre.

edge.rationale: Weighted squared deviations are calculated after deviations from the mean are found.
edge.failure_signal: Learner averages raw deviations or ignores probabilities when calculating variance.

edge.rationale: Unit interpretation follows from the meaning of standard deviation for a discrete random variable.
edge.failure_signal: Learner gives standard deviation in squared units or treats it as unitless.
